description: Phase 9h — name-resolution error propagation dual-target pin. Closes the three cross-target error-surface findings from the 2026-04-21 fuzz campaign (tests/fuzz/results/2026-04-21-README.md). Bug A: INSERT VALUES with a bare identifier must raise EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE on both builds (leap-rust previously aborted via SIGABRT). Bug B: SELECT with an unresolved column under GROUP BY must raise STORAGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND (or the alias-equivalent COMPILE_UNKNOWN_COLUMN) on both builds. Bug C: a deep recursive CTE whose fixed-point cannot complete must raise RUNTIME_RECURSIVE_CTE_LIMIT, not COMPILE_UNKNOWN_TABLE. All prior phase fixtures MUST stay green.

cases.name: bug-a-insert-values-bare-identifier
cases.description: INSERT INTO t VALUES (x) with a bare identifier x that is not a column of t (INSERT VALUES is a no-table context). Fuzz reproducer: `INSERT INTO t VALUES (x)` after `CREATE TABLE t(a INT)`. Expected: EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE on BOTH targets, NEVER a SIGABRT. leap-c already emits this; leap-rust must converge.

cases.name: bug-a-insert-values-bare-identifier-multicol
cases.description: Multi-column INSERT VALUES tuple where one entry is a bare identifier: `INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, q)` on `CREATE TABLE t(a INTEGER, b INTEGER)`. The unresolved `q` must raise EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE, not abort. Shape-matches fuzz reproducer crash_0001 from the 2026-04-21 campaign.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);

cases.name: bug-a-insert-values-multirow-bare-identifier
cases.description: Multi-row INSERT VALUES (Phase 6w) where a later tuple contains a bare identifier. Fuzz reproducer crash_0002 shape: `INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2), (s)`. Expected: EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE, not a crash.

cases.name: bug-a-insert-values-bare-identifier-column-name
cases.description: Subtle variant: the bare identifier shares the target column's name. `INSERT INTO t VALUES (a)` on `CREATE TABLE t(a INTEGER)`. Even though `a` is the target column, INSERT VALUES does NOT bind column names in the tuple expression scope (no such SQL feature in v1 — matches Phase 6j/6w semantics). Expected: EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE on BOTH builds, consistent with bug-a's base case.

cases.name: bug-a-insert-values-bare-identifier-arithmetic
cases.description: Bare identifier inside an arithmetic expression in INSERT VALUES — exercises the recursive descent through BinaryOp. `INSERT INTO t VALUES (q + 1)`. Expected: EVAL_COLUMN_WITHOUT_TABLE, not abort.

cases.name: bug-b-select-unresolved-col-group-by
cases.description: SELECT with a bare unresolved identifier in the projection list, under a GROUP BY that references a real column. Canonical fuzz reproducer: `SELECT i, SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k` on `t(k TEXT, v INTEGER)`. leap-c emits STORAGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND; leap-rust must NOT abort. Pre-fix leap-rust panicked at `check_all_column_refs must have resolved outer-scope ref` inside the grouped-aggregated scan-emit phase. The harness's error_name_aliases rule accepts COMPILE_UNKNOWN_COLUMN as the Rust-native spelling.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT i, SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k;

cases.name: bug-b-select-unresolved-col-group-by-no-aggregate
cases.description: Same GROUP BY scaffold, but the projection has no aggregate — bare unresolved column alone plus the GROUP BY key. Exercises the pre-aggregate bare-column-collection path at the same point. Expected: STORAGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND (or alias-equivalent).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT i FROM t GROUP BY k;

cases.name: bug-b-select-unresolved-col-group-by-having
cases.description: Unresolved column in HAVING (post-projection evaluation, same alias-scope rules). `SELECT SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k HAVING i > 0`. Expected: STORAGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND for the unresolved `i` in HAVING.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k HAVING i > 0;

cases.name: bug-b-select-unresolved-col-group-by-order-by
cases.description: Unresolved column in ORDER BY under GROUP BY — exercises the collect_bare_columns_not_in_group_by walker over the order-by term tree. Expected: STORAGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, not abort.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT k, SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k ORDER BY i;

cases.name: bug-c-recursive-cte-deep-self-reference
cases.description: Deep recursive CTE that references itself and must surface RUNTIME_RECURSIVE_CTE_LIMIT on both builds. Direct fuzz reproducer from 2026-04-21 README. leap-c trips the 1000-iter cap inside the fixed-point loop; leap-rust's driver did not implement the fixed-point loop end-to-end and previously raised COMPILE_UNKNOWN_TABLE for `c`. Phase 9h pins RUNTIME_RECURSIVE_CTE_LIMIT as the user-visible error regardless of whether the generator trips the cap or detects the self-reference pre-iteration. The Phase 6bl fixture `phase6bl.json` already pins the same kind for the infinite case `SELECT n+1 FROM c` (no WHERE).

program.sql: WITH RECURSIVE c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM c WHERE n < 1000000) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c;

cases.name: regression-valid-insert-values-literal
cases.description: Regression guard — non-error INSERT VALUES with a literal still works. Ensures the Phase 9h fix does not over-reject valid inputs.

cases.name: regression-valid-insert-values-arithmetic
cases.description: Regression guard — INSERT VALUES with a literal arithmetic expression (the Phase 6j widening) still works after Phase 9h pin. No column references, no error.

cases.name: regression-valid-group-by-bare-col-in-group-key
cases.description: Regression guard — Phase 6bo bare-column GROUP BY behaviour unchanged: a bare column that IS in the GROUP BY key set still resolves correctly and emits the key value.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT k, SUM(v) FROM t GROUP BY k ORDER BY k;

cases.name: regression-valid-group-by-bare-nonkey-col
cases.description: Regression guard — Phase 6bo bare-column-not-in-GROUP-BY semantics unchanged: a real column that is NOT in the GROUP BY key still emits a last-row-seen value. The Phase 9h pin only rejects UNRESOLVED identifiers, not unaligned-but-resolvable ones.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t(k TEXT, v INTEGER);
SELECT v, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY k;
